newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Iceland economy seen cooling in 1997-98-OECD.
newsitem.headline: Iceland economy seen cooling in 1997-98-OECD.

text.p: Iceland's economy is expected to cool down over the next two years after expanding briskly in 1996, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said.
Currently economic activity was expanding at the most rapid rate since the mid-1980s with growth fueled by marine exports and expansion of the country's sole aluminium smelter.
The OECD said Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in market prices climbed by an estimated 5.4 percent in 1996 but is seen slowing to 3.3 percent in 1997 and 2.9 percent in 1998.
"After growing rapidly in 1996, the economy is expected to cool off gradually over the next two years," the OECD said.
Investment growth in 1996, bolstered by the expansion of the Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG aluminium smelter and strengthening fish exports was expected to continue.

The OECD said substantial real wage gains were likely to push private consumption and inflation higher with the result of imminent national wage negotiations and their effect on the economy a key uncertainty.
